question_text: If 1, ω, ω² are the cube roots of unity, then prove that 1/(1 + 2ω) + 1/(2 + ω) = 1/(1 + ω).

mark_split.label: Simplify the right side and compare

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — how the left side reduces, how the right side reduces, and why they are equal.
insider_note: Both sides come to −ω, and the question is not finished until the right side is reduced as well. The first mark is spotting that 2 + 5ω + 2ω² = 2(1 + ω + ω²) + 3ω = 3ω.

steps.label: Simplify the left side to −ω
steps.margin_note: First mark. Adding the two fractions gives 3(1 + ω) over 2 + 5ω + 2ω². Split that denominator as 2(1 + ω + ω²) + 3ω = 3ω, so the left side is (1 + ω)/ω = −ω²/ω = −ω.

steps.why: Every ω question is the same two facts: ω³ = 1 (so high powers of ω reduce) and 1 + ω + ω² = 0 (so any two of 1, ω, ω² can be replaced by minus the third). The reduction is the mark; the arithmetic after it is short.
common_mistakes: Multiplying out the denominator and not spotting 2(1 + ω + ω²) inside it.

steps.label: Simplify the right side and compare
steps.margin_note: Second mark. On the right, 1 + ω = −ω², so 1/(1 + ω) = −1/ω² = −ω/ω³ = −ω. Both sides are −ω; write that line, because the comparison is the mark.

steps.why: The right side also reduces to −ω once 1 + ω is replaced by −ω² and the fraction is multiplied by ω/ω. Both sides equal, so the identity is proved.
common_mistakes: Leaving 1/(−ω²) unsimplified and not seeing it equals −ω.
